text: Superstition is a leftover habit of an older faith. When one religion gives way to another, the old one rarely leaves the field. Its beliefs and rites stay, but the old meaning is lost, so the habit is called superstition. One example is the old worry about eating horse. The Celts once held the horse in honor, and the custom of refusing its meat is a small echo of that sacred past. In the same way, the banshee and other fairy beings were part of an older belief, but today they are read as plain superstition. What is called superstition is the small shape of a forgotten faith.
